pos.personaBrief: Happel's Feyenoord 3-man midfield and Brugge/Hamburg quick two-touch passing show a side that dictated play, with 'a 5-1 over 1-0' risk appetite and breakaways as a bonus.

pro.personaBrief: The Blizzard cites tidy, quick passing with two-touch training and fast breakaways, while the midfield trio drove the game; no long-ball culture.

est.personaBrief: Zonal marking, defined 4-3-3 roles and a midfield trio point to a structured side, with Moulijn dropping and fullbacks pushing on within the shape.

lar.personaBrief: Games unfolded from the central midfield trio, but attacking full-backs gave width; wingers were not the main route.

blo.personaBrief: Early pressing at Brugge and a pressing 4-3-3 at Hamburg with a high line; 'don't forget the pressing'.

mar.personaBrief: Zonal marking at Feyenoord (Van Duivenbode) and 'man-marking means eleven donkeys' make him a clear zone coach.

pla.personaBrief: At Brugge the other team had to adapt to Happel's side; he imposed his approach, with tactical tweaks like the asymmetric 1983 final setup.

res.personaBrief: He preferred 5-4 to 1-0, went for broke with an extra striker, and played to win away, though he was pragmatic about winning.

sis.personaBrief: Strict collective roles, a tactical coach who built around drilled midfield but with talented players; he wanted everyone to work.

jog.personaBrief: Hard-running pressing football with technical passers like Van Hanegem and Jansen; intensity required, no room for walkers.

bas.personaBrief: At Brugge he offloaded 30-somethings for energetic youngsters, but he was not an academy builder and signed players.

lid.personaBrief: Absolute authority: training starts when he says, stars demoted, distance from players, discipline over friendship.
